speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: asked	the Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (a) what is the role of Nanyang Polytechnic International Pte Ltd and its relationship with Nanyang Polytechnic; and (b) how does the Ministry intend to address the findings of the Auditor-General in its Report for FY2015/2016.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, what was "internal function" is now put into a company.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: These are potential revenue-generating activities and, through a subsidiary, NYP intends to make it a self-sustaining activity.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: To ensure alignment between NYPi's activities and NYP's mission and objectives, selected board members and staff of NYP also serve as board members of NYPi.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This reflects the intention of NYP to closely supervise, guide and manage the activities of NYPi, which is its fully-owned subsidiary, and there are two points I would like to highlight here.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The activities performed by NYPi are to fulfil the mission and objectives of NYP, rather than NYPi's own objectives.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This is why it is fully-owned by NYP.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: No profits flow out to any third party.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And the NYPi staff do not partake in any profit-sharing scheme.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It is now a company, a separate legal entity.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, all rental and charges by NYP imposed on NYPi should have been made based on market rates or with subsidies explicitly approved and recorded in NYP's accounts.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I have to emphasise a key point in all of these, at the risk of repeating myself, so that AGO's observations are not misunderstood.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: There was no personal interest involved on the part of the directors of NYP and NYPi, and no leakage of money to any third parties.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: When AGO referred to some NYP board of governors (BOG) members as having "vested interests", it merely referred to the fact that they would have had an interest in ensuring NYPi performs well in NYP.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It had nothing to do with them having any personal or financial interests in NYPi.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And it was, indeed, in NYP's interest that NYPi did well.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This is, hence, completely different from a situation where you have an entity where a director or staff owns a stake in an outside party vendor and then provides services or sells products to the entity for a fee or revenue.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I have three supplementary questions, just to follow up on the initial question that I filed.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Did the excess funding of about $8.38 million given to NYPi cause any disruptions to programmes or operations of NYP itself?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: My second question is whether sufficient steps have been taken to ensure that current and future members of the BOG are adequately informed and reminded of the need to be above-board and ensure proper financial controls and governance?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Third, are any actions taken against NYP BOG members who had so-called vested interests, as well as NYP's staff involved and whose lack of oversight may have caused these lapses to occur?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I will answer the last one first which is whether there were any actions taken against staff or directors.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I think a mistake was made but it is one, as I have mentioned earlier, that does not involve profits flowing out to any third party.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: It does not involve any fraud or personal gains.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: However,  we have to take every step that we can to improve the corporate governance framework, because if you want to set up a subsidiary and a company, notwithstanding it is fully-owned, it is a separate legal entity and there has to be a proper governance framework.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: To answer the Member's second question, we are taking additional steps to brief every single polytechnic and Institute of Technical Education about all these rules.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: NYP, as we speak, is drafting a framework.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: It has a Board of Directors' meeting in October, and all those steps and the new framework will be approved by October.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As for the so-called excess funding of $8.38 million, to put this into context, NYPi was previously a division and department with a budget, when it also received all these so-called subsidies.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: It is just that, after it became a separate entity, NYP continued to provide the help to allow it to function well.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But it should now be a lot more transparent.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: There is nothing wrong with subsidising your own subsidiary when it is 100% owned and carrying out your mission and objectives.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: What NYP ought to have done was to make those subsidies and help transparent, and NYP is doing so, so as to ensure a better corporate governance framework.
